highlights.title: Introducing Claude Opus 5
highlights.summary: Anthropic has announced Claude Opus 5, the latest and most capable model in the Claude family. Developers using Claude Code should explore how this new model can enhance their coding workflows with improved reasoning and task completion. Check the Anthropic blog for details on capabilities and how to enable it in your setup.

highlights.title: Claude Code v2.1.232 Released – Subagent Forking On by Default
highlights.summary: Subagent forking is now enabled by default, meaning a 'fork' subagent inherits the full conversation and prompt cache, making multi-agent workflows faster and more efficient. You can now type '@' in the prompt to mention and reference another Claude session by name. Non-teammate agent spawns in interactive sessions also now run in the background by default, reducing interruptions.

highlights.title: Claude Code v2.1.233 Released – GitLab MR Support & User Identity Forwarding
highlights.summary: Claude Code now supports GitLab merge request URLs in the '--worktree' flag and the agents view, where merge requests display as '!N' for easy identification. An opt-in 'forward_user_identity' setting has been added for Anthropic upstreams, letting proxies receive the signed-in user's identity as headers. This is especially useful for teams running Claude Code in managed enterprise environments.

highlights.title: Claude Code is Leaking Real Email Addresses as a User-Agent String in curl Commands
highlights.summary: A security issue has been flagged where Claude Code includes the signed-in user's real email address in the User-Agent header of curl commands it generates, potentially exposing personal data in logs or to third-party servers. Developers should be aware of this until a fix is confirmed, especially when running Claude Code in shared or production environments. Monitor the linked GitHub issue for updates and patches.

highlights.title: Maximizing the Value of Your Claude Code Sessions
highlights.summary: Anthropic's official blog post shares strategies for getting the most out of each Claude Code session, covering best practices for prompting, session management, and workflow structure. This is a great read for developers who feel their sessions lose focus or context mid-task. Implementing even a few of these tips can significantly improve the quality and efficiency of your Claude Code interactions.

highlights.title: Show HN: Graft – Claude Code Hooks That Cut grep Tokens by 42%
highlights.summary: Graft is an open-source tool that uses Claude Code hooks to optimize how code search (grep) operations are performed, reducing token usage by 42% in testing. For developers concerned about API costs or hitting context limits, this kind of efficiency gain can make a real difference in large codebases. Check out the GitHub repo to integrate Graft's hooks into your own Claude Code setup.

highlights.title: The Ultimate Claude Code Tutorial (Beginner to Pro)
highlights.summary: This YouTube tutorial walks developers through Claude Code from the very basics all the way to advanced workflows, making it ideal for anyone just getting started or looking to level up their skills. It covers setup, core commands, and practical coding scenarios you can follow along with in VS Code. Bookmark this as a reference you can return to as you grow more comfortable with Claude Code.

highlights.title: Claude Code New Features, Explained
highlights.summary: This YouTube video breaks down the latest Claude Code features in an accessible, easy-to-follow format, helping developers quickly understand what's changed and how to use new capabilities. It's a great companion to reading changelogs, offering visual demonstrations instead of just text descriptions. Watch this alongside the recent v2.1.232 and v2.1.233 release notes to see the new features in action.

tips_of_the_day: Use the new '@' mention feature in Claude Code v2.1.232 to reference another active session by name — this is a powerful way to coordinate context across parallel tasks without copy-pasting.

Before running Claude Code in any environment where curl commands are executed against third-party APIs, double-check your User-Agent headers in the terminal output to ensure no personal data like your email is being exposed until the current security issue is patched.

Take advantage of subagent forking (now on by default) by breaking large coding tasks into smaller subtasks and letting Claude Code spin up background agents — you'll get results faster and keep your main session focused.
